$comment: Pairs of enum values that render as the same word in a locale, and are
PERMISSIONS pairs a bare scope with its VIEW_ form and translates both
as the noun; ALERT_SEVERITY carries WARN and WARNING from two different
emitters. The STATUS pairs are the ones worth revisiting: ACKNOWLEDGED
and CONFIRMED, and in FR DENIED and REJECTED, are distinct states a
user cannot tell apart. They are pinned because they predate the check,
JOB_TITLE carries two spellings of one job twice over: LAB_SCIENTIST is
the legacy DB value for LABORATORY_SCIENTIST (the enum says so), and
HOSPITAL_ADMIN predates HOSPITAL_ADMINISTRATOR. Both pairs are the same
job, so one label is the honest answer and the English keeps the two
spellings only because the enum does. Retiring the legacy constants is a
data migration, not a wording change.
